android.status: feasible - source-supported + prior art; runtime PoC required

aether.binary_availability: official release binaries: aether-android-arm64 / armv7 / x86_64 (v2.4.0, .sha256 published)
aether.embedding: build libaether for Android targets from source with cargo-ndk (crate-type includes staticlib/cdylib); boring+quiche cross-compile required - not verified here
aether.process_mode: possible (PattNG prior art runs the aether binary on Android; ship as executable nativeLibraryDir entry); exec from app data dir is blocked by noexec on modern Android
aether.mark_support: --mark works (SO_MARK) with root/CAP_NET_ADMIN only - not available to a normal VpnService app
aether.evidence: release assets list; DOCS.en.md; OPENWRT.en.md references PattNG; egress.rs cfg(linux/android)

zeptun.binary_availability: zig build android + scripts/build_android.sh: libzeptun.so/.a for armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86, x86_64 + libzeptun-jni.so (ndk-build, APP_PLATFORM android-24, 16 KB load-segment alignment for Android 15+)
zeptun.jni: dev.zeptun.Zeptun: nativeStart(service, fd, config) / nativeStop / nativeVersion / nativeCounter; protect callback calls VpnService.protect(int) for every upstream socket; engine runs on its own pthread (zeptun_run)
zeptun.routing: WITHOUT root: VpnService.Builder owns routes (addRoute/addAllowedApplication/addDisallowedApplication); auto_route must be OFF; mobile build compiles out the route module by default. WITH root: /dev/tun + policy rules + package rules via /data/system/packages.list + fwmark bit 0x200000
zeptun.evidence: README 'Build/Android'; docs/wiki/Android.md; build.zig (mobile default for android); src/jni/zeptun_jni.c; src/route/android.zig

android.vpn_integration: Android VpnService: Builder.establish() fd passed to zeptun (ZEPTUN_DEVICE_FD / --tun-fd); foreground service required for running VPN; onRevoke -> nativeStop
android.loop_prevention: 1) zeptun protect() callback protects zeptun upstream sockets; 2) Aether's own sockets are NOT protected by that callback -> addDisallowedApplication(own package) is the recommended app-level exclusion (covers aether + app UI + zeptun at once); with root, --mark 0x200000 or --exclude-uid also possible
android.dns: VpnService.Builder.addDnsServer (in-tunnel DNS address); zeptun dns hijack/fake-ip on top
risks: aether-on-Android cross-compile not verified here (no toolchain per audit rules)
single-process JNI engine (one tunnel at a time)
Android 15 16 KB alignment requirement is handled by zeptun's build; aether Android builds must match (cargo/rustc default aligns 16 KB on aarch64 since mid-2024 - verify per target)
memory ceiling per app process on low-end devices

windows.status: feasible - source-supported; runtime PoC required; elevation + loop-prevention are the open questions

aether.binary_availability: official release aether-windows-x86_64.zip (v2.4.0); arm64 Windows NOT in release list
aether.embedding: cdylib -> DLL possible from source; cross-compile with x86_64-pc-windows-gnu/msvc toolchain - not verified here
aether.mark_support: --mark DOES NOT WORK on Windows (warning + unmarked sockets; egress.rs cfg linux/android)

zeptun.binary_availability: zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows-gnu (+ msvc) and arm64; Wintun DLLs vendored for amd64/arm64/x86/arm; released Windows archives already contain wintun.dll
zeptun.device: Wintun adapter via LoadLibraryEx/GetProcAddress; GUID pinning (zeptun_set_adapter_guid / --tun-guid) keeps adapter identity across reinstalls
zeptun.routing_dns: IP Helper (routes + DNS); upstream sockets bound with IP_UNICAST_IF; --strict-route installs a WFP session (permits engine + tunnel interface, can block IPv6 and port 53 outside)
zeptun.evidence: README 'Build/Windows'; docs/wiki/Building.md + Routing.md; src/device/wintun.zig; src/route/windows.zig; src/route/wfp.zig; third-part/wintun/*

windows.vpn_integration: No OS VPN framework for third-party apps: the app creates a Wintun adapter and installs routes (zeptun auto_route) - requires Administrator (adapter creation + route changes + firewall rules)
windows.loop_prevention: SO_MARK unavailable; zeptun protects only its own sockets (IP_UNICAST_IF). Aether outbound MUST bypass via: (a) zeptun flow-callback returning ZEPTUN_FLOW_DIRECT for Cloudflare WARP/API destination ranges (engine-level, cross-platform), and/or (b) route exclude list for WARP anycast ranges (104.16.0.0/12-ish pools + 162.159.0.0/16 + 188.114.96.0/22 + 172.64.0.0/13). PoC MUST verify no loop
windows.dns: IP Helper DNS settings; zeptun dns hijack option; strict-route WFP blocks port 53 outside tunnel while hijacked
risks: admin elevation flow (run-as-admin or service wrapper) unverified
Windows port reservation can break aether --bind (aether prints a netsh hint)
Wintun driver redistribution licensing is permissive for API-only use (zeptun wiki), still needs legal review
aether arm64-windows build absent from releases
windows.architectures: x86_64 (primary), arm64 (zeptun only until an aether build exists)

linux.status: verified feasible - highest confidence; zeptun's own 189-check integration suite runs on Linux

aether.binary_availability: official releases: x86_64, x86_64-musl, aarch64, aarch64-musl (v2.4.0 list includes aarch64 + arm64), armv7-musl
aether.embedding: libaether.a/.so from source; also prebuilt-engine use
aether.mark_support: --mark works (SO_MARK, root or CAP_NET_ADMIN); probe at startup fails fast

zeptun.binary_availability: make / zig build; 13 Linux architectures as static musl binaries in releases; systemd unit included
zeptun.device: /dev/net/tun, multi-queue, vnet header, TSO/USO offloads, NAPI; io_uring or epoll; auto_route installs table 2022 + policy rules 9000-9009; upstream fwmark 0x2022; nftables auto-redirect (system stack); netns mode; route monitoring via netlink
zeptun.evidence: README; docs/wiki (Routing, Stacks); src/route/linux.zig; scripts/netns_integration.sh; docs/wiki/Testing.md

linux.vpn_integration: TUN requires root or CAP_NET_ADMIN (device creation + routes). Aether --mark 0xff + 'ip rule add fwmark 0xff lookup main priority 100' (priority < 9000) is the documented loop-prevention pair; engine-level flow-callback DIRECT is the portable alternative
linux.dns: full set: --dns-address, --dns-hijack, --fake-ip, --dns-upstream, --systemd-resolved (resolvectl handover with ~. routing domain, reverted on exit)
risks: Aether env-var mutation constrains embedded single-instance use
auto_redirect requires system stack (userspace default on mobile builds)
linux.architectures: x86_64, aarch64 (both engines); more via musl cross builds
linux.verified_by_tests: zeptun integration suite: every stack mode, both io backends, 1 and 4 queues, direct and SOCKS5, offloads on/off, UDP over TCP, fake-IP, strict routing, auto-redirect, elastic rotation, netns - on Linux (docs/wiki/Testing.md)

macos.status: feasible - source-supported; NEPacketTunnelProvider or privileged-helper decision needed

aether.embedding: static lib from source; the aether C API was built for exactly this kind of client (DOCS.en.md 'Using Aether as a library')
aether.mark_support: --mark DOES NOT WORK on macOS (warning; egress.rs)

zeptun.binary_availability: make xcframework produces macOS slice; universal CLI binary in releases
zeptun.device: utun; kqueue; split default routes; exclusions via previous gateway; upstream sockets bound IP_BOUND_IF; route socket monitoring

macos.vpn_integration: Two options: (a) NEPacketTunnelProvider (system extension; entitlement + user approval; sandboxed; tunnel fd or EXTERNAL callbacks) - App Store path; (b) CLI/root service with utun + auto_route (CLI binary needs sudo)
macos.loop_prevention: SO_MARK unavailable; same as Windows: flow-callback DIRECT for WARP ranges and/or route excludes; IP_BOUND_IF protects only zeptun sockets
macos.dns: route socket based; hijack/fake-ip options apply
risks: sandbox of the provider process may restrict aether's file/state paths

ios.status: feasible with additional native integration - NEPacketTunnelProvider REQUIRED; process spawning is forbidden; memory limit is the top risk

aether.binary_availability: NO iOS release binary; must cross-compile libaether (staticlib) for ios-arm64 from source (boring/quiche cross-compile) - NOT verified in this audit
aether.embedding: the C API exists specifically for the iOS use case ('This is what the iOS client needs', DOCS.en.md); aether_core_start(job-polled) is the intended entry
aether.mark_support: irrelevant - routing is owned by NetworkExtension, not marks
aether.evidence: DOCS.en.md 'Using Aether as a library'; ffi.rs; Cargo.toml crate-type

zeptun.binary_availability: scripts/make_xcframework.sh -> Zeptun.xcframework with ios-arm64 + ios-simulator (arm64/x86_64) + macos slices; Package.swift for SwiftPM
zeptun.device: NEPacketTunnelProvider: pass tunnelFileDescriptor (utun fd found by walking open fds) as ZEPTUN_DEVICE_FD, or ZEPTUN_DEVICE_EXTERNAL with packet callbacks inside packetFlow
zeptun.preset: mobile preset (1 queue, no offload, userspace stack, 24 MB memory budget) for the extension's tight memory limit
zeptun.evidence: docs/wiki/Apple.md (NetworkExtension Swift example); README 'Build/iOS and macOS'

ios.vpn_integration: NEPacketTunnelProvider + NEPacketTunnelNetworkSettings (addresses, includedRoutes, dnsSettings, mtu); entitlements: network-extension + packet-tunnel-provider capability; App Store VPN apps require review; the extension process hosts BOTH engines (aether + zeptun linked into the extension)
ios.loop_prevention: NE routing is per-flow owned by the system: the provider's own traffic does not re-enter its tunnel by construction (the tunnel has no routes back into itself); flow-callback DIRECT remains available as defense in depth
ios.dns: NEDNSSettings in tunnel settings + zeptun hijack/fake-ip
risks: packet-tunnel-provider memory limit (~50 MB class) vs aether (quiche+boringssl+tokio) footprint - MEASURE in PoC
iOS cross-compile of aether not verified here (needs Xcode; audit had no Apple toolchain)
extension + UI process split requires IPC (App Group / XPC) between Flutter UI and provider
tor feature (arti) on iOS is heavy - build WITHOUT the tor feature
